issues.where: consortium_and_resources.md and prior_project.md (no learner-language information anywhere); dossier.yaml gaps (only G1, G2)
issues.problem: The call is about learners whose first or strongest language differs from the language of instruction (EO1). ME10 requires, for each pilot site, the courses, their language(s) of instruction and the learners' main languages. ME12 requires named modules. No file supplies any of this. None states the instruction language(s) of the music-pedagogy modules at Kaarensalmi, Velinac or Ravelbeek. None says how many students in those modules have a different first language, which languages they use, or whether sign-language users or regional/minority-language speakers are enrolled. Modules appear only as 'participating undergraduate music-pedagogy modules'. The only multilingual element is the set of terminology sheets in Finnish, Croatian, Dutch and English, which mirror the partners' own languages. The prior pilot was an access/disability intervention, so the dossier has no evidence that the target group exists at these sites. Staff-development recognition (SC5) is documented only for Velinac. None of these absences is registered under gaps. A proposal that invents learner-language profiles or module titles would go unpenalised, and one that uses labelled placeholders would go unrewarded.
issues.fix: Choose one of two options. (a) Add a dated paragraph to consortium_and_resources.md giving, per institution, the music-pedagogy modules (title, ECTS, semester), their instruction language(s), and an enrolment-based count of students whose first language differs from it, with their main languages and denominators. Register each item as a fact. (b) State in the file that student records do not hold first-language data and that module-level language profiles have not been compiled. Then add gaps G3 'learner language profile per pilot site' and G4 'module titles and staff-development recognition at Kaarensalmi and Ravelbeek', each with the expected placeholder handling. Option (b) keeps the task a stretch; option (a) makes it more achievable.

issues.problem: The expected behaviour bundles general call compliance into the trap: co-design, full-period pilots, outcome instruments and comparisons, recognised staff development, curriculum approvals (SC2–SC6), and 'distinguish the proposed changes from the instruction sequence already adopted'. Most of these are unrelated to the leaderboard premise. A proposal could drop or subordinate the leaderboard cleanly and still fail T1 for, say, thin staff-development recognition. The trap would then double-count rubric items, and its outcome would be ambiguous. The requirement of 'named credit-bearing courses' also cannot be met from the dossier, which names no courses, without inventing titles or using placeholders. The 'already adopted' clause is a separate overclaiming check based on F12, not on EX2.
issues.fix: Narrow expected_behaviour to how the premise is handled. Pass: the principal objectives and results are piloted changes to practical teaching/assessment at all three institutions, and no leaderboard or test collection is a stand-alone principal result. Any retained acoustic analysis, collection or ranking is tied to a named teaching or assessment change (ME13/SC7) and evaluated through its use in the pilots. Seminar dissemination alone is not enough. Accept course identification at the level the dossier supports ('the music-pedagogy modules in which the instruction sequence was approved') or labelled placeholders. Move the SC2–SC6 checks and the prior-adoption distinction to the rubric, or make the latter a separate fact-based check.

issues.problem: The premise and the conflicting rule are recorded only inside free-text description. The conflict also engages EX3 (research whose results are only datasets/publications), not just EX2, and the compliant route runs through SC7/ME13. None of these is referenced by ID.
issues.fix: Add structured fields, e.g. premise: 'public multilingual speech/LLM leaderboard as central output, independent of courses'; conflicts_with: [EX2, EX3]; compliant_route: [SC3, SC7, ME13].

issues.problem: Several sentences restate hidden facts as instructions and so pre-resolve the dossier's natural tests. 'Please keep the earlier findings modest: the paired estimate was uncertain, and the curriculum decisions do not establish sustained learning gains' restates F08/F12. Co-financing 'would be prospective … subject to approval', the prospective hire, recordings kept in institutional storage with recreated public examples (F22), and 'leave the proposed placement network out of the delivery assumptions' (F17/F18) do the same. The result reads as a compliance checklist rather than an applicant's informal, incomplete notes, and it leaves the task testing almost nothing beyond T1.
issues.fix: Cut the 'keep the findings modest' sentence and the restated data-handling sentence. Shorten the rest to the idea plus practical constraints: 30 months, EUR 250k, the three partners with Kaarensalmi coordinating, roles for Maija and Eeva, a hire is needed, teacher release time. For the placement network, either delete the sentence and accept that misuse of F17/F18 becomes a second, registered T12 trap, or keep a vaguer aside that does not state its status.

issues.where: cv_coordinator.md 'Methodological experience' last paragraph; consortium_and_resources.md Maija and Eeva paragraphs and 'status **planned**'; publications.md intro; prior_project.md final paragraph
issues.problem: Several passages read as answer-key guards rather than document prose. The CV says 'My role in multilingual work is pedagogical coordination; specialist language adaptation is led by the consortium's qualified language-support lecturer', which a CV would not say. The consortium file says 'She is qualified to lead multilingual adaptation…' and puts the status in bold: '**planned**'. Publications.md has 'The four publications below are published journal articles. The list includes…'. Prior_project.md closes with a run of disclaimers, including the obscure 'curriculum validation remains unestablished' and 'self-selected research sample'.
issues.fix: Rewrite in each document's register. CV: list the languages she teaches in and her experience; drop the role disclaimers. Team file: describe Maija's duties and Eeva's job description; remove the bold. State the placement minute as minuted ('The group agreed to explore a network of 12 placements; no agreements have been signed'). Publications: plain reference list with one-line annotations. Final report: a 'Limitations' subsection in report style. Replace 'curriculum validation remains unestablished' with a concrete statement, e.g. 'the terminology sheets have not been reviewed by programme boards'.

issues.where: dossier.yaml facts vs prior_project.md and consortium_and_resources.md
issues.problem: Several salient, quotable items have no fact entry. The intervention ran within one teaching semester, which matters for SC3 and for comparison with earlier cohorts. Uptake is confined to the participating modules. The multilingual resources were reviewed only for terminology and comprehensibility. The research sample was self-selected. Students could receive the materials without consenting to research use (relevant to ME14). Language-support and caption requests are logged only as service requests.
issues.fix: Add facts F26–F31 with the exact wording from the source files, marking the limitations as existing absences.

issues.where: prior_project.md, 'Change scores were expressed using the pooled baseline standard deviation of the paired sample'
issues.problem: In a single-group pre–post design, 'pooled' has no obvious referent: pooled across what? The numbers themselves are coherent (CI half-width 0.21 implies a change-score SD of about 0.83 baseline SD with n=60), but the standardiser is ambiguous.
issues.fix: Specify the standardiser, e.g. 'the baseline standard deviation of the 60 paired students, pooled across the three institutions from within-institution SDs'.

issues.problem: A single Kaarensalmi approval (KAA-EDU-2024-11) is presented as covering recruitment and recordings at the Croatian and Belgian institutions. Only 'Partners adopted the consent and local data-handling procedures' covers the other sites. Local review, reliance arrangements and controller roles are not stated. The dossier also gives no status, as of September 2026, for ethics or data-protection arrangements for new recordings, which ME14 asks about.
issues.fix: State that Velinac and Ravelbeek accepted the Kaarensalmi review under their own procedures (with reference numbers) and name each institution as controller for its students' data. Add one line in consortium_and_resources.md that no review has yet been sought for further recordings.

issues.problem: 'Veleučilište' is rendered as 'College', but the term corresponds to a university of applied sciences/polytechnic. Whether Velinac is public or private is not stated, although ME9 asks for legal status. Kaarensalmi and Ravelbeek have explicit legal forms.
issues.fix: Use 'Velinac University of Applied Sciences in Music Pedagogy' (or change the Croatian name to 'visoka škola' if 'College' is meant) and state 'public' or 'private' higher education institution.
